note: Adults with T1D on insulin: streptozotocin-diabetic rats (dapagliflozin 2008; empagliflozin plus insulin 2012) predicted the insulin-sparing glucose lowering that DEPICT and EASE confirmed, but no rodent model the class relied on reported ketoacidosis, the harm that cost the class its US indication (CRLs 2019 and 2020) and its EU one (withdrawn 2021); rats reproduced euglycaemic DKA only in 2019, post hoc.
label: T1D (SGLT2i adjunct)

engagement.note: Dapagliflozin cut blood glucose up to 55% in insulin-deficient STZ rats, the filed model; no patient comparison yet.
engagement.short: Dapagliflozin lowers glucose in STZ rats
engagement.quote: The C-aryl glucoside 6 (dapagliflozin) was identified as a potent and selective hSGLT2 inhibitor which reduced blood glucose levels in a dose-dependent manner by as much as 55% in hyperglycemic streptozotocin (STZ) rats.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract verbatim (Europe PMC). FDA pharmacology review for NDA 202293 confirms the STZ rat as the filed insulin-deficient model: 'The STZ-treated rat is a model of insulin deficient diabetes ... dose-dependent reduction in blood glucose which was statistically significant at 0.03 and 0.1 mg/kg'.
engagement.judgement: Track opens on the first SLC5A2-selective use in an insulin-deficient animal. Han 2008 (https://doi.org/10.2337/db07-1472) is the fuller pharmacology paper (renal glucose excretion in normal and diabetic rats); Luippold 2012 (https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1463-1326.2012.01569.x) later ran empagliflozin with insulin in the same STZ-rat system and is kept on this track (same model, same prediction).

engagement.note: Remogliflozin etabonate raised urinary glucose excretion and lowered post-load glucose in 10 insulin-pump T1D patients, the rat glycosuria readout.
engagement.short: Glycosuria and glucose fall in T1D patients
engagement.quote: RE significantly increased urine glucose excretion and reduced the rise in plasma glucose concentration after oral glucose.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Single-dose crossover in 10 subjects; sibling product on the model side (rats were dosed with dapagliflozin); no ClinicalTrials.gov record found for this study (searched by intervention and by term 'remogliflozin', only T2D records returned), so registry_date is null.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: Han 2008 reported that dapagliflozin 'acutely induced renal glucose excretion in normal and diabetic rats'; Mudaliar 2012 shows the same proximal readout (urinary glucose excretion) in T1D patients with a member drug, remogliflozin etabonate. Earliest public member-drug PD datum in T1D, so it dates the cell (rule 6). Whether remogliflozin's own rodent package (Fujimori 2008) included STZ rats was not checked, hence product_in_model false.
engagement.magnitude_basis: urinary glucose excretion and plasma glucose, direction only

engagement.note: Empagliflozin abolished glomerular hyperfiltration in Akita mice (397 to 255 uL/min); in hyperfiltering T1D patients it cut GFR 33 mL/min, same drug.
engagement.short: Akita hyperfiltration result held in patients
engagement.quote: During clamped euglycemia, hyperfiltration was attenuated by -33 mL/min/1.73m(2) with empagliflozin in T1D-H, (GFR 172±23-139±25 mL/min/1.73 m(2), P<0.01).
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level on both sides. Cherney's reference list (checked in the v2 pass) cites STZ-rat tubular-hypothesis work, not Vallon's Akita paper, so the pairing is mine. Vallon 2014 epub 2013-11-13, Cherney 2014 epub 2013-12-13: both public in 2013, hence year 2013; print 2014; NCT01392560 results posted 2014-06-17.
engagement.judgement: Separate track: a different model (genetic Akita mouse) making a different prediction (hyperfiltration, not glucose) with the product itself (Vallon 2014, https://doi.org/10.1152/ajprenal.00520.2013: empagliflozin 'completely prevented the diabetes-induced increase in glomerular filtration rate (GFR) (255 vs. 397 μl/min)'). Readout is downstream physiology (GFR). Magnitude within 2x on fractional GFR fall: mouse -36% (397 to 255), patients -19% (172 to 139). Academic model, not in any filed package (model_filed false). Not a retrodiction: the mouse paper preceded the patient result.
engagement.magnitude_basis: fractional fall in GFR in hyperfiltering subjects (mouse -36%, patients -19%)

engagement.note: Dapagliflozin itself, the filed STZ-rat drug: glucosuria rose 88 g/24 h at 10 mg in 70 T1D patients, PK as in T2D.
engagement.quote: Glucosuria increased by 88 g/24 h (95% CI 55 to 121) with dapagliflozin 10 mg and decreased by -21.5 g/24 h (95% CI -53.9 to 11.0) with placebo.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; registry NCT01498185 results posted 2017-02-10 (checked). Epub 2014-09-30, print March 2015.
engagement.judgement: Strengthens the 2012 entry with the product the rat model actually used (product_in_model true) and a placebo-controlled design (n=70, 2 weeks, 1-10 mg). The abstract also states 'Pharmacokinetic parameters were similar to those observed in patients with type 2 diabetes', which is why no separate T1D dose entry is made.
engagement.reason: Rat glycosuria readout held in T1D
engagement.magnitude_basis: 24-h urinary glucose excretion, direction only (rat values in g/kg not comparable)

dose.note: Rats gave an mg/kg dose-response (0.01-0.1 mg/kg) but no exposure target; T1D doses were the T2D doses, so no model-to-patient dose comparison exists.
dose.quote: The C-aryl glucoside 6 (dapagliflozin) was identified as a potent and selective hSGLT2 inhibitor which reduced blood glucose levels in a dose-dependent manner by as much as 55% in hyperglycemic streptozotocin (STZ) rats.
dose.confidence_note: FDA pharmacology review (NDA 202293) text searched: STZ-rat glucose lowering 'statistically significant at 0.03 and 0.1 mg/kg', no exposure or margin stated for an insulin-deficient setting. Luippold 2012 abstract gives rat doses in combination with insulin but no exposure target (full text paywalled).
dose.judgement: Untested rather than an empty list: the STZ rat was used for dose-response in the filed package, but no model stated an exposure, occupancy or regimen target for T1D. Patient doses were carried over from T2D (dapagliflozin 5/10 mg in DEPICT-1/2; empagliflozin 10/25 mg plus a 2.5 mg arm added for safety in EASE; ipragliflozin 50 mg in Kaku 2019); Henry 2015 showed T1D PK matched T2D PK, a human-to-human comparison. The one dose-dependent clinical finding that mattered, DKA at empagliflozin 10/25 mg but not 2.5 mg (Rosenstock 2018) and EMA's restriction of dapagliflozin to 5 mg, had no stated model margin, so under decision 16 the harm is counted once, in safety, and dose stays untested.

efficacy.note: Glucose fell 55% in rats with no endogenous insulin: the premise that SGLT2 inhibition adds glucose lowering on top of insulin in T1D.
efficacy.quote: The C-aryl glucoside 6 (dapagliflozin) was identified as a potent and selective hSGLT2 inhibitor which reduced blood glucose levels in a dose-dependent manner by as much as 55% in hyperglycemic streptozotocin (STZ) rats.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract verbatim; STZ-rat study confirmed in the FDA pharmacology review text for NDA 202293.
efficacy.judgement: The explicit adjunct-to-insulin T1D prediction came four years later in the same system: Luippold 2012 (STZ rats, empagliflozin with insulin glargine or insulin implants over 28 days) concluded 'Empagliflozin combined with low-dose insulin showed comparable glucose-lowering efficacy to treatment with high-dose insulin' and 'is an efficacious adjunctive-to-insulin therapy with the clinical potential for the treatment of T1DM'. Same model, same prediction, so one track; the NOD-mouse work (Powell 2015) was with sotagliflozin, not a member, and is left out.

efficacy.note: DEPICT-1 primary endpoint met: HbA1c -0.42/-0.45 points vs placebo at 24 weeks on dapagliflozin 5/10 mg added to insulin in 778 T1D patients.
efficacy.quote: At week 24, both doses of dapagliflozin significantly reduced HbA1c compared with placebo (mean difference from baseline to week 24 for dapagliflozin 5 mg vs placebo was -0·42% [95% CI -0·56 to -0·28; p<0·0001]
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the quote is the first clause of the findings sentence, cut at 34 words. NCT02268214 results posted 2018-03-29 (checked); epub 2017-09-14.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me with Luippold 2012 (model_src), which predicted insulin-sparing glucose lowering in STZ rats; dapagliflozin itself was dosed in the same model (Meng/Han 2008), so product_in_model is true although the insulin-combination experiment used empagliflozin. Earlier patient data were not scored as efficacy: Perkins 2014 (NCT01392560, single-arm open-label, HbA1c 8.0 to 7.6%) had GFR as its registered primary; Henry 2015 (NCT01498185) had safety as its stated primary objective, and its registry-listed 7-point glucose measure at day 7 did not separate from placebo (differences -1 to -7 mg/dL, CIs about ±35 mg/dL, n about 14 per arm), a 2-week study not designed for efficacy, so it neither sets `same` nor `contra`. Magnitude is direction only: rat HbA1c units do not scale to the 0.4-point clinical effect. Outcome trials: none.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: HbA1c change vs placebo; rat HbA1c effect not scalable

patient_trials.quote: At week 24, both doses of dapagliflozin significantly reduced HbA1c compared with placebo

The ipragliflozin group demonstrated a significant decrease in HbA1c from baseline to end of treatment versus the placebo group: adjusted mean difference (AMD) -3.8 mmol/mol (95% confidence interval [CI] -6.2, -1.5) or - 0.36% (95% CI -0.57, -0.14; P = 0.001).

efficacy.note: EASE-2/3 with the model's own drug: empagliflozin 10/25 mg cut HbA1c 0.54/0.53 points vs placebo at 26 weeks in 1,707 T1D patients.
efficacy.quote: The observed largest mean placebo-subtracted glycated hemoglobin reductions were -0.28% (95% CI -0.42, -0.15) for 2.5 mg, -0.54% (-0.65, -0.42) for 10 mg, and -0.53% (-0.65, -0.42) for 25 mg (all P < 0.0001).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. NCT02580591 (EASE-3) results posted 2018-11-02, NCT02414958 (EASE-2) 2018-11-20 (checked); epub 2018-10-04.
efficacy.judgement: Strengthens 2017: this is the exact product-and-regimen Luippold 2012 modelled (empagliflozin added to insulin in STZ rats), with the primary HbA1c endpoint met at 10 and 25 mg and a smaller effect at 2.5 mg. Kaku 2019 (ipragliflozin 50 mg, 175 Japanese T1D patients, HbA1c -0.36%, NCT02897219, no registry results posted) extends the same direction to a third member. Direction only, as above.
efficacy.reason: Insulin-sparing glucose lowering held in patients
efficacy.magnitude_basis: HbA1c change vs placebo; rat HbA1c effect not scalable

patient_trials.quote: The observed largest mean placebo-subtracted glycated hemoglobin reductions were -0.28% (95% CI -0.42, -0.15) for 2.5 mg, -0.54% (-0.65, -0.42) for 10 mg, and -0.53% (-0.65, -0.42) for 25 mg (all P < 0.0001).

efficacy.model: Exposure-response simulation of empagliflozin 2.5 mg built on EASE-2 patient data (M-EASE-1 semi-mechanistic, M-EASE-2 descriptive)
efficacy.note: Pharmacometric models built on EASE-2 (10/25 mg) simulated 2.5 mg HbA1c -0.29% at 26 weeks; EASE-3 had observed -0.28%, known since 2018.
efficacy.quote: The HbA1c benefit of low-dose empagliflozin directly observed in the EASE-3 trial was confirmed by two modelling and simulation approaches.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMID 31858718, epub 2020-01-21, print 2020-03); EASE-3 NCT02580591 results posted 2018-11-02. The 2021 companion paper (Johnston 2021, PMID 33918261, https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics13040485) calls the models supportive evidence for the 2.5 mg dose; whether they were in the T1D sNDA is unverified because the November 2019 EMDAC briefing document is not retrievable, so model_filed is null.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): the models were developed 'independently of data from EASE-3' but after EASE-3's 2.5 mg result was public (Rosenstock 2018), and the paper's stated aim is to confirm it; so retro, not same, although the simulation matched the observed value within 2x (-0.29% vs -0.28%). Scored in efficacy because the simulated quantity is the primary endpoint (placebo-corrected 26-week HbA1c), not an exposure target; it therefore does not change the stz-rat dose cell. Comparison stated by the source. Single entry, as for the Perry retrodiction track, because the first use is the retrodiction. The model's clinical purpose, supporting 2.5 mg as a lower-DKA dose, was not accepted: FDA's advisory committee voted 14-2 against empagliflozin 2.5 mg in November 2019 and a complete response followed in 2020 (press coverage, tier 5, not scored); no prospective prediction from the model has since been tested in patients.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: placebo-corrected 26-week HbA1c change at empagliflozin 2.5 mg: simulated -0.29% versus observed -0.28% in EASE-3

patient_trials.quote: The observed largest mean placebo-subtracted glycated hemoglobin reductions were -0.28% (95% CI -0.42, -0.15) for 2.5 mg, -0.54% (-0.65, -0.42) for 10 mg, and -0.53% (-0.65, -0.42) for 25 mg

safety.note: Insulin-deficient rats were read for glucose only; the dapagliflozin FDA pharmacology review and the Luippold 2012 abstract never mention ketones or acidosis.
safety.quote: The C-aryl glucoside 6 (dapagliflozin) was identified as a potent and selective hSGLT2 inhibitor which reduced blood glucose levels in a dose-dependent manner by as much as 55% in hyperglycemic streptozotocin (STZ) rats.
safety.confidence_note: Text search of the FDA pharmacology/toxicology review for NDA 202293 (271 kB of extracted text, STZ and ZDF rat studies present): zero occurrences of ketone, ketosis, ketoacidosis, beta-hydroxybutyrate or acidosis. Luippold 2012 checked at abstract level only (paywalled).
safety.judgement: The model was silent on a harm the species can show (rat plasma beta-hydroxybutyrate is routinely measured). Devenny 2012 (https://doi.org/10.1038/oby.2012.59) did report raised fasting BHBA on dapagliflozin in diet-induced obese rats, but as a fuel shift in an insulin-replete model that the class never carried into its insulin-deficient models; it is a different system and is not scored here.

safety.note: Adjudicated DKA 4.3%/3.3% on empagliflozin 10/25 mg vs 1.2% placebo in EASE; the STZ-rat work with the same drug plus insulin reported no ketone signal.
safety.quote: Adjudicated diabetic ketoacidosis occurred more with empagliflozin 10 mg (4.3%) and 25 mg (3.3%) but was comparable between empagliflozin 2.5 mg (0.8%) and placebo (1.2%).
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; EASE-3 registry results 2018-11-02, EASE-2 2018-11-20 (checked). Model-side silence verified in the FDA review text; Luippold 2012 abstract only.
safety.judgement: Called contra on the model's silence, as in the ad-amyloid safety cell. Dating: the first unequivocal member-drug T1D trial datum is EASE (epub 2018-10-04), followed by DEPICT-1 at 52 weeks (Dandona 2018, https://doi.org/10.2337/dc18-1087: definite DKA 4.0%, 3.4% vs 1.9%, epub 2018-10-23). Earlier signals were not member-specific or not separated: Henry 2015 (2 weeks) 'No diabetic ketoacidosis occurred'; the FDA Drug Safety Communication of 2015-05-15 was class-level FAERS cases; Peters 2015 (https://doi.org/10.2337/dc15-0843, full text checked) describes canagliflozin cases, with dapagliflozin and empagliflozin appearing only in its reference list; DEPICT-1 at 24 weeks (Dandona 2017) reported definite DKA in 1%, 2% vs 1%. Kaku 2019 saw no DKA in 175 patients on ipragliflozin 50 mg over 24 weeks, too small to offset. Regulatory course, all on DKA: EC approved dapagliflozin 5 mg for T1D (BMI >= 27) in March 2019 and Japan the same month; FDA issued a complete response letter for dapagliflozin in July 2019 (AstraZeneca press release; no advisory committee was found for dapagliflozin in T1D); FDA's Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee voted 14-2 against empagliflozin 2.5 mg in November 2019 and a CRL followed in March 2020 (press coverage, tier 5, not used for status); AstraZeneca withdrew the EU/UK T1D indication on 2021-10-25 citing commercial reasons (MHRA Drug Safety Update). Contra persists; the 2019 rat reproduction is its own track.

safety.note: Built after the clinic knew: dapagliflozin caused euglycaemic ketoacidosis in rats only with insulinopenia plus volume depletion, reproducing the patient DKA.
safety.quote: Here we show that the SGLT2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) dapagliflozin promotes ketoacidosis in both healthy and type 2 diabetic rats in the setting of insulinopenia through increased plasma catecholamine and corticosterone concentrations secondary to volume depletion.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level plus the v2 check's verified full-text details (rats with insulin <125 pM 'indicating type 1 diabetes' were excluded; authors caution that the weighting of dehydration vs insulinopenia may differ between rat and human). Open access.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): the paper opens from the clinical concern ('concerns have been raised about their potential to induce euglycemic ketoacidosis') and reproduces it, so retro, not same. Separate track from the STZ rat: a different system (48-h-fasted healthy and STZ-nicotinamide/high-fat T2D rats, not a T1D model) built to a different prediction (ketoacidosis, not glucose). Partial because the model needed both insulinopenia and dehydration and excluded T1D-range insulin levels. No prospective prediction from this model has since been tested in patients.
safety.reason: Rodents silent on DKA until 2019 retrodiction

safety.model: Diet-induced obese rat, insulin-replete (dapagliflozin, 38-day weight-loss study)
safety.note: Dapagliflozin raised fasting beta-hydroxybutyrate in insulin-replete DIO rats, a ketone signal the filed STZ rat never read; no T1D patient comparison yet.
safety.short: Dapagliflozin raises ketones in obese rats
safety.quote: Fasting BHBA was elevated in the 1 mpk, 5 mpk, and 5 mpk PF-V groups.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract verbatim (Europe PMC, PMID 22402735, epub 2012-03-08, print 2012-08). Not in the dapagliflozin NDA 202293 pharmacology review (zero hits for diet-induced, DIO, obese rat or hyperphagia), so model_filed false.
safety.judgement: Own track under the identity rule: a different system (insulin-replete obese rat in a weight-loss study) with a different prediction (ketone rise) from the filed STZ rat, which read glucose only. Opened untested at first public use; the rats were not diabetic and the paper makes no clinical ketone claim.

safety.model: Diet-induced obese rat, insulin-replete (dapagliflozin, 38-day weight-loss study)
safety.note: DEPICT-2: adjudicated DKA 2.6%/2.2% on dapagliflozin 5/10 mg vs 0% placebo in 813 T1D patients; the DIO rat's ketone rise, same drug, held in direction.
safety.quote: There were more adjudicated definite diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) events with dapagliflozin: 2.6%, 2.2%, and 0% for dapagliflozin 5 mg, dapagliflozin 10 mg, and placebo, respectively.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMID 30026335, epub 2018-07-19, print 2018-09; NCT02460978 results posted 2018-11-06). The pairing is mine: the rat readout was fasting BHBA in non-diabetic obese rats, the patient readout adjudicated DKA incidence, so direction only.
safety.reason: Insulin-replete rat ketone rise matched DKA
safety.judgement: Same, direction only: the model's own drug raised fasting ketones in rats (2012) and raised DKA incidence in T1D patients; there is no shared quantity, so no magnitude beyond direction. Dated to the first member-drug T1D trial with a clear DKA direction for dapagliflozin: Henry 2015 (2 weeks) reports 'No diabetic ketoacidosis occurred'; DEPICT-1 at 24 weeks (Dandona 2017) 1%/2%/1% is ambiguous; DEPICT-2 (epub 2018-07-19) precedes EASE (Rosenstock 2018, epub 2018-10-04) and DEPICT-1 52-week (Dandona 2018, https://doi.org/10.2337/dc18-1087, epub 2018-10-23, definite DKA 4.0%/3.4% vs 1.9%), which concur. No source states the comparison; Perry 2019 does not cite Devenny. The model was never relied on for T1D and predicted a ketone rise, not acidosis: the readout was a side observation in a weight-loss study, hence medium confidence and no neg call.
safety.magnitude_basis: fasting beta-hydroxybutyrate rise in rats versus adjudicated DKA incidence in patients; no shared quantity

safety.model: Zucker diabetic fatty (ZDF) rat, empagliflozin with or without metformin, 28 days (NDA 206111 nonclinical review)
safety.note: FDA's Synjardy pharmacology review: 28-day ZDF rats on empagliflozin 3 mg/kg had unremarkable ketone bodies (data not shown); no T1D comparison yet.
safety.quote: Day 14 and day 28 plasma c-reactive protein (CRP), adiponectin and ketone bodies were unremarkable (data not shown).
safety.confidence_note: Tier 2 review text (sources/206111/206111Orig1s000PharmR.txt line 557; reviewer signature 2015-04-15, public on approval in 2015). 'Data not shown' scores at low confidence (brief rule 2). GLP combination study in male ZDF rats, a hyperinsulinaemic T2D model; empagliflozin 3 mg/kg alone and with metformin 300 mg/kg.
safety.judgement: Own track: a different system from the STZ rat and the DIO rat, filed for a member drug, with a stated negative on ketones rather than silence. Opened untested at the review's public date; the study predates it but its date is not given in the review text.

safety.model: Zucker diabetic fatty (ZDF) rat, empagliflozin with or without metformin, 28 days (NDA 206111 nonclinical review)
safety.note: EASE: adjudicated DKA 4.3%/3.3% on empagliflozin 10/25 mg vs 1.2% placebo; the ZDF rat on the same drug called ketone bodies unremarkable.
safety.short: Stated no-ketone call contradicted by DKA
safety.quote: Adjudicated diabetic ketoacidosis occurred more with empagliflozin 10 mg (4.3%) and 25 mg (3.3%) but was comparable between empagliflozin 2.5 mg (0.8%) and placebo (1.2%).
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMID 30287422, epub 2018-10-04, print 2018-12; NCT02580591 results 2018-11-02, NCT02414958 2018-11-20). Low because the model side is 'data not shown' in an insulin-resistant T2D model and the pairing with T1D patients is mine.
safety.reason: Negative ketone call failed in T1D
safety.judgement: Contra, not untested: the review states a negative ketone finding with the member drug, and rats can show the harm (the DIO rat did with dapagliflozin in 2012), so the species could have shown it. Counted once here as a stated prediction; the STZ-rat track scores its own silence separately. The ZDF rat is hyperinsulinaemic, the opposite physiological state to T1D; that lowers confidence but does not change the status, which scores what the model said against what patients showed. Dated to EASE, the first member-drug T1D trial with empagliflozin DKA; DEPICT-2 (dapagliflozin, epub 2018-07-19) is the same year with a different member, and the same-drug pairing is preferred. No later source reverses the patient signal.

safety.model: Exposure-response simulation of empagliflozin 2.5 mg built on EASE-2 patient data (M-EASE-1 semi-mechanistic, M-EASE-2 descriptive)
safety.note: An Emax exposure-response model built on EASE-3 predicted the EASE-2 week-26 BHB rise (small, dose-related, far below 1.5 mmol/L); both trials' BHB data were public since 2018.
safety.quote: It was developed based on data from EASE‐3 and qualified by predicting the BHB changes in the EASE‐2 study population.
safety.confidence_note: Full text (PMC7064984, Results and Discussion: simulated medians 'closely approximated the values directly observed in the EASE‐2 and EASE‐3 trials'; 'minor blood BHB level elevation ... was confirmed'). EASE-2 NCT02414958 results posted 2018-11-20; Rosenstock 2018 (PMID 30287422) published both trials' BHB. DKA itself was not modelled (low event numbers).
safety.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): fitted to EASE-3 BHB and checked against EASE-2 BHB, both public before the 2020 paper, so retro, not same. Scored in safety because the readout is the ketone rise, the class's DKA-risk biomarker; the paper states DKA events could not be modelled, so it makes no DKA-incidence prediction. Same system as the efficacy entry; comparison stated by the source.
